title: Move the jobs off the web server

entities.name: web-1
entities.about: The web server. It runs the app and, today, every background job too.

entities.name: jobs-1
entities.about: A new machine that would run background jobs only.

entities.name: scheduler
entities.about: The process that starts timed jobs, like a nightly export.

entities.name: workers
entities.about: Processes that take jobs off the queue and run them.

entities.name: queue
entities.about: The Redis list where jobs wait for a worker.

terms.about: Let running jobs finish and take no new ones before stopping.
A worker's time-limited claim on a job; when it runs out, another worker may take the job.
A job that failed too often and is set aside for a person to look at.
The moment jobs stop running in the old place and start in the new one.

intro: Page loads on `web-1` slow down every night while the export runs. This grill decides whether the background jobs move to their own machine, and how to move them without losing a job.
Each concept on the left is one part of the decision. Questions wait until what they depend on is answered.

parts.title: Why move
parts.summary: Whether the jobs leave `web-1` at all.

parts.title: What moves
parts.summary: Which pieces go to `jobs-1` and which stay.

parts.title: No lost jobs
parts.summary: How a job survives a crash or a bad run.

parts.title: The cutover
parts.summary: How the switch happens and how to undo it.

steps.heading: Move the jobs at all
prose:
### What goes wrong
The nightly export takes most of `web-1`'s memory for about forty minutes, and page loads slow down while it runs.

### Move them
Move the jobs to their own machine, `jobs-1`. The web server then only serves pages.

### Add memory
Give `web-1` more memory. Cheaper today, but the next heavy job brings the slowdown back.

question.title: Move the jobs
question.ask: Should background jobs move from `web-1` to a new `jobs-1`?

options.label: Move them to `jobs-1`
options.effect: Page loads stop depending on job load. One more machine to run.

options.label: Keep them; add memory to `web-1`
options.effect: No move. The slowdown returns with the next heavy job.

now.note: takes most of its memory for forty minutes

b.value: normal until the next heavy job

steps.heading: Does the scheduler go too
prose: The `scheduler` only starts jobs; the `workers` run them. Left on `web-1`, it keeps a reason to deploy jobs code there, and a `web-1` restart would skip a timed job.

question.title: Scheduler
question.ask: Should the `scheduler` move to `jobs-1` with the `workers`?

options.label: Both move
options.effect: `web-1` holds no jobs code at all.

options.label: Only the workers move
options.effect: Smaller move; `web-1` still restarts the timed jobs.

steps.heading: Where the queue lives
prose: The `queue` sits in the Redis on `web-1`, next to the session cache. Moving it means a second Redis to back up; keeping it means `jobs-1` reaches across the network for every job.

options.label: Keep it on `web-1`
options.effect: Nothing new to run. Jobs wait on one network hop.

options.label: Its own Redis on `jobs-1`
options.effect: Jobs and pages fully apart, one more thing to back up.

steps.heading: When a worker dies mid-job
prose: Today a job taken by a worker that crashes is simply gone. A lease fixes that: the worker claims the job for a few minutes and renews the claim while it runs, so a dead worker's jobs come back to the `queue`.

question.title: Leases
question.ask: Should each worker hold a 5-minute lease on the job it runs?

options.label: 5-minute leases
options.effect: A crashed job is retried within five minutes.

options.label: No leases
options.effect: Simpler, and a crash still loses the job.

steps.heading: When a job keeps failing
prose: With leases, a job that crashes its worker comes back forever. After a few tries it should stop and wait for a person.

question.title: Dead letters
question.ask: Should a job that fails 5 times go to dead letters?

options.label: Dead letters after 5 tries
options.effect: A bad job stops after five tries; someone looks at the list.

options.label: Retry forever
options.effect: Nothing to look at, and a bad job can block a worker for good.

steps.heading: Stopping the old workers
prose: At the cutover, the `workers` on `web-1` may be halfway through jobs. Drained, they finish and stop; stopped hard, their jobs come back through the leases from Q4.
Where the `queue` lives (Q3) decides whether `jobs-1` sees the same jobs from the first second.

options.label: Drain, then start
options.effect: No job runs twice. A few minutes with nothing running.

options.label: Start `jobs-1`, then stop `web-1`
options.effect: No pause, and a job may run twice.

steps.heading: Undoing it
prose: If `jobs-1` misbehaves in the first week, the fastest way back is to start the old `workers` again.

question.title: Rollback
question.ask: Should `web-1` keep its workers installed but stopped for a week?

options.label: Remove them at the cutover
options.effect: Clean at once; rolling back is a deploy.

next: The answers settle the move plan; the cutover gets a date once Q6 and Q7 are answered.
